messages:
Jules (People Ops): Threading the remote/hybrid + offsite Q&A follow-up from today's all-hands. Focused on parents, accommodations, and cancellation rules. Reply here with edge cases.
Roxanne (Eng): Two quick ones: if a parent needs to bring a child to HQ for a one-off emergency, is there a place to do that quietly?
Kara (Office Ops): We have a "quiet room" on floor 4 for short-term use (max 4 hours). Book via /rooms and select "family support". Facilities will prioritize emergency bookings.
Vik (Finance): Are dependent-care expense policies different for offsites vs regular travel? Trying to give clear guidance to managers.
Jules (People Ops): Dependent-care reimbursement applies equally for mandatory business travel, onboarding visits, and offsites. Pre-approval required; submit receipts in Expensify under "dependent-care". Cap: $160/day unless pre-approved.
Roxanne (Eng): If someone needs to bring a caregiver (e.g., nanny) for a week-long collab, will Redwood cover their travel?
Ethan (CEO): We won't cover caregiver travel as a general rule. Exceptions possible for ADA accommodations or documented medical needs — People Ops + Legal will evaluate on a case-by-case basis.
Roxanne (Eng): OK thanks.
families-bot: Policy snippet: ADA accommodation requests must be submitted 10 business days before travel when feasible: https://intranet.redwood/accommodations
Jules (People Ops): For flexible schooling schedules / school holidays: teams should be flexible with core overlap days during major school breaks. Managers please document any expected changes in team calendars.
Vik (Finance): Clarifying per-diem for offsite family-inclusive events (rare)  if family members join optional social events, those are not reimbursable unless explicitly approved.
Kara (Office Ops): On hoteling: we'll be piloting "family-friendly" desk blocks near lactation rooms and quiet rooms starting May 2. Book with tag "family-friendly".
hoteling-bot: New booking tag available: "family-friendly"  8 desks reserved on weekdays for May pilot. Book at /hoteling.
Roxanne (Eng): What about last-minute cancellations for offsites due to weather or other forced closures? Refund policy?
Jules (People Ops): If the company cancels, Redwood covers any non-refundable employee costs. If an individual cancels, we reimburse per existing travel policy only with manager approval and valid reason. Use the travel form to request exception.
Ethan (CEO): One note: leaders should avoid scheduling mandatory in-person work during major regional school holidays where possible. Use async options or give extra notice.
Vik (Finance): For dependent-care, add "dependent-care" as an expense category in Expensify by Apr 30. Finance will fast-track true emergency claims on a case-by-case basis.
Jules (People Ops): Action items: 1) People Ops to publish family-travel FAQ and ADA accommodation flow by Apr 25; 2) Facilities to enable family-friendly hoteling pilot May 2; 3) Finance to add dependent-care category by Apr 30. I'll post links when live.
Roxanne (Eng): Appreciate the clarity.
Kara (Office Ops): If anyone has suggestions for the family-friendly pilot layout, DM me floor plans.
Jules (People Ops): Thanks everyone 64F will keep this thread updated. If you have individual needs, DM People Ops or file an accommodation request.
